text:
jess: heads up — planning to push release/2026.03.20 to prod in the 10:00-11:00 UTC change window. quick permissions check: i added 2 contractors to the release squad but they report they can't trigger deploy. can someone confirm who can actually press the deploy button?
ryan: i think we tightened the deployer group last week. contractors shouldn't have the role unless explicitly added. who are the two?
jess: alex_c and samir_t — both onboarded last week. alex got 'temp-deploy' in okta but samir didn't. alex still sees a 403 when calling the deploy endpoint.
amal: security here — we rotated the deployer-boundary and added an MFA requirement for prod deploys (JIT only). contractors need to request JIT via the portal or use opsctl for a short-lived grant. we didn't auto-include the contractor org.
jess: opsctl snippet i used during staging:
```
opsctl iam request-jit --principal "okta://alex_c" --role "redwood-prod-deployer" --duration 60m --reason "release 2026.03.20 canary" 
```
jess: alex says opsctl returns "permission denied: must have mfa enrolled" even though he enrolled.
amal: if opsctl says MFA missing it's usually the Okta factor sync lag. ask them to re-login to the SSO portal and re-run. if still broken i can run a one-off grant but i need approval from oncall.
mike-oncall: i'm oncall now — i can approve a one-off grant for emergencies but prefer JIT through opsctl. how critical is this?
jess: not critical yet — can hold canary for 30m, but want to avoid manual grants for every contractor. also need to capture in release notes that deployers list changed.
ryan: long term we should add contractors to a separate ephemeral deployer group that requires owner sign-off. short term: amal, can you confirm the exact okta attribute we check for MFA so we can tell alex what to re-do?
amal: we check SSO factor status + device trust flag. tell alex to clear all active sessions and reauthenticate, then run opsctl again. if still 403 ping me and i'll run a one-off grant (audit will record it).
sec-bot: [audit] manual_grant_requested by amal for principal okta://alex_c at 2523456845 — pending approver: mike-oncall
mike-oncall: approving manual grant for alex_c for 45m. note in release notes: "manual JIT grant applied for alex_c due to Okta sync lag" :thumbsup:
jess: thanks. i'll delay the canary start by 10m and update the changelog. also adding a reminder to release playbook to include a quick okta MFA reauth step.
ryan: can we add a small checklist item to the deploy-bot that auto-checks deployer group membership and MFA status before allowing `prod-deploy`? low effort but would reduce these pings.
amal: agree — i'll write a short policy RFC and ping infra.
jess: if anyone sees other gaps (role pinning, release notes, or who signs off), reply here. otherwise i'll proceed after alex confirms the grant worked.
deploy-bot: Deploy request created (id=dc-9876, ref=release/2026.03.20). status=waiting-for-approval
jess: alex confirmed via DM: opsctl worked after reauth. proceeding with canary in 10. will post results in this thread.
ryan: nice — can you paste the one-line we should add to the release notes?
jess: "Ops: Manual JIT grant (45m) issued for okta://alex_c due to Okta MFA sync lag; recommend reauth prior to deploy."
amal: logging that to the security audit trail now.
sec-bot: [audit] manual_grant_approved by mike-oncall for okta://alex_c at 2523456898 — duration 45m — reason: release canary
jess: thanks all. follow-up action: amal to propose ephemeral contractor-deployer group; ryan to add pre-deploy checks to deploy-bot. i'll attach the release note before final push.
